title: docs(qa): a checklist item drives the fresh-install order (os migrate apply, then the first os serve), and validation-rule-type-matrix drops its red-until-#24782 text
body:
Fixes #25054
Clause-②: no

Two items in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/` and nothing else: no product code, test, pin, changeset or `RUNNER.md`. `areas/integration-system.json` (open in PR #25045) is untouched.

## 1. New item `cli.fresh-install-migrate-apply-first` (`areas/cli.json`, revision 1)

- **What it drives:** an empty file database, `os migrate apply --yes` first, then the first `os serve`, in one environment, as a deploy script runs them.
- **Oracle:** the boot (acceptance[1]). The serve reaches `✓ Server is ready` (not DEGRADED), `/api/v1/health` answers 200, and the output has no organization-ownership refusal. The marker is read at its own layer (acceptance[0]): the `sys_migration` row `adr-0131-organization-ownership`, read through SQLite after the apply and before any boot, then again after the boot, where it must be unchanged.
- **Release:** `since: "v18.1"`. The change for #24827 is `.changeset/24827-migrate-apply-birth-marker.md`, a `minor` changeset pending on `main`, so it ships in 18.1.0. `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` says a run against 18.0.0 records the refusal as 18.0.0's known behaviour, not as a FAIL of the item. Measured: the fix commit `19484af538` is not an ancestor of the `@objectstack/cli@18.0.0` tag commit `06cab4849a` (exit 1). Control leg, the commit 50 behind that tag: exit 0. The checkout is not shallow.
- **Pins:** `fixtures.knownGaps[1]` says why the fix's two pins score no clause (RUNNER rule 6). `apply.organization-ownership-birth.integration.test.ts` runs `MigrateApply` in-process, and `schema-migrate.birth-after-flush.test.ts` runs with no kernel. Neither spawns the CLI or boots `os serve`. So the item has no `automated` ref, and both clauses are driven live.
- **Why a new item.** No existing item's scope covers this order. I read the titles and scopes of `platform-core.json` and `cli.json` at `688052e147`:

| item | its scope | why the order does not belong there |
|---|---|---|
| `platform-core.v18-boot-refusals` | a 17.x-shaped database | its revision 6 says the order "is not added here" |
| `cli.organization-ownership-ceremony` | upgrading a database that 17.x or an 18.0 pre-release created | it never uses an empty database |
| `cli.migrate-plan-apply-json` | plan and apply on a database a prior `os dev` boot synced (its `fixtures.requires[0]`) | it never uses an empty database and never boots after the apply |
| `platform-core.boot-health`, `cli.dev-boot-contract` | the `os dev` boot | that boot creates the tables and writes the birth marker itself, so the order cannot arise |
| `cli.scaffold-first-run` | the published scaffold, booted by `os start --artifact` | it has no `os migrate apply` |

## 2. `records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix` (`areas/records-forms.json`, revision 6 to 7)

- `fixtures.knownGaps[1]` is removed, and the closing "Red until #24782 lands" is removed from `acceptance[5].clause`. `knownGaps[1]` itself asked for both edits once the change for #24782 merged. It merged as PR #25051 (`72518d20f5`), per the `domain:engine` pointer 6308955528 on seat post #6023. No other field changed.

Each edited item gets one `revision` bump and one `history` row. The new item starts at revision 1 with one row. A scripted editor made the edits: text edits inside each target item's own span, then a re-parse asserting that every other item, every top-level key, and the bytes outside the spans are unchanged, and that the target matches the intended edit exactly. The history rows carry the placeholder ref `#PENDING-25054`, because this PR had no number yet. The next commit on this branch replaces it with this PR's number and changes nothing else.

## Live readings on `main` (base `688052e147`, CLI built from this worktree)

### Fresh-install order: first evidence for the new item

The showcase was run from this PR's worktree. Run directory under the session scratchpad: `fresh.db` absent before the run (`test ! -e` on it and on its `-wal` and `-shm`). Environment for both commands: `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:RUN/fresh.db`, `OS_HOME=RUN/home`, and `OS_AUTH_SECRET` and `OS_SECRET_KEY` set to fresh random values. The boot also had `OS_PORT=41873`.

1. `os migrate apply --yes`: exit **0**. It printed `✓ Created/extended 107 table(s): 107 table(s) to create, 0 column(s) to add.` and `[organization-ownership] a datastore created from empty: birth marker written (shape generation 1, platform 18.0.0).`
2. The marker row, read through `node:sqlite` before any boot: `id adr-0131-organization-ownership`, `verified_at 2026-10-21T06:54:23.840Z`, `applied_at null`, `blocking 0`, `advisory 0`, `details {"birth":{"shapeGeneration":1,"platformVersion":"18.0.0","createdAt":"2026-10-21T06:54:23.840Z"}}`. This is the only row with that id.
3. `os serve -p 41873` (started with `setsid`): it printed `✓ Server is ready` with `Mode: production` and `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuard` among the plugins. `GET /api/v1/health` answered 200 10 s after the start, and `GET /api/v1/ready` answered 200. Refusal greps over the output: `carries no organization-ownership marker` 0, `refuses to start` 0, `os migrate organization-ownership` 0.
4. The marker row after the boot: one row, identical to step 2. The process group was stopped and port 41873 is free.

| item (revision) | clause | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli.fresh-install-migrate-apply-first` (1) | acceptance[0] | pass | apply exit 0, created-tables line, the row in steps 2 and 4 |
| `cli.fresh-install-migrate-apply-first` (1) | acceptance[1] | pass | `✓ Server is ready`, health 200, 0/0/0 refusal greps |

Item verdict: **pass**.

### Verification re-run of `records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix` acceptance[5]

The boot was the canonical checklist boot: `pnpm -C WORKTREE/examples/app-showcase exec objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p 41874 -d file:SCRATCH/data.db` with `OS_PORT=41874` exported. The run signed in as the seeded admin and authored the two scratch objects of `fixtures.requires[2]` with `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_vr_probe` and `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_vr_probe_err`, which both answered 200. Then it followed steps[6]:

- `POST /api/v1/data/qa_vr_probe {"title":"abc"}` answered **201**, and the re-read found 1 row (`title abc`).
- Exactly **one** server-log line names `qa_unevaluable_warn`, across the whole log: `Validation rule 'qa_unevaluable_warn' (warning): the rule could not be evaluated (runtime: int() type error: cannot convert to int) — write proceeded: the rule is advisory, so it was not applied to this write`. Lines naming the rule that contain `write rejected`: 0. Lines that contain `fails closed`: 0.
- Control: `POST /api/v1/data/qa_vr_probe_err {"title":"abc"}` answered **400** `VALIDATION_FAILED`, with `fields[0].constraint` `{rule: qa_unevaluable_err, reason: unevaluable}`. The re-read found 0 rows. Its log lines say `— write rejected: a rule that cannot be evaluated fails closed, it is never skipped`, which is true here.

| item (revision run) | clause | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix` (6) | acceptance[5] | pass | 201 + re-read, the single log line quoted above, control 400 + empty re-read |
| `records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix` (6) | acceptance[0] to [4] | skipped | outside this verification re-run |

This is a verification re-run, so it files no run record (RUNNER, Run records). Both servers were stopped by process group, and `examples/app-showcase/.objectstack`, which the boots wrote into the worktree, was deleted.

It comes right after the same boot's `datasource 'showcase_external': connect denied by policy (schemaMode 'external': …)`. A migrate run serves nothing, so the line's consequence does not describe this run. This is passed to the seat through the report on #25054.
